title: Believers called just and holy over against the wicked
source_text: XI. Ab utraque vero fideles in Scriptura frequenter justi sanctique nominantur, & quidem opposite ad impios & peccatores, a quibus illos Scriptura justorum titulo distinguit. Ut quum apud Petrum dicitur, Oculi Domini super justos, & aures ejus in preces eorum: vultus autem Domini super facientes mala, 1 Pet. 3. 12. Item, Si justus vix salvatur, impius & peccator ubi comparebit? 1 Pet. 4. 18. Neque fide-les in genere solum justi sanctique nuncupantur; sed & sigillatim ex fidelibus multi hoc titulo insigniuntur, ut exempli gratia, Noe qui dicitur fuisse vir justus & integer in generationibus suis, Gen. 6. v. 9. & Lot, quem Petrus Apostolus justi nomine desi-gnat, 2 Petr. 2. v. 7, 8. item Joseph ab Arimathaea, Luc. 23. 50.
pass_a_gloss: But from both, believers in Scripture are frequently named just and holy, and indeed over against the wicked and sinners, from whom Scripture distinguishes them by the title of the righteous. As when it is said in Peter, The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears toward their prayers; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil (1 Peter 3:12). Likewise, If the righteous is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear? (1 Peter 4:18). Nor are believers only in general called just and holy; but also individually many of the faithful are marked with this title—for example Noah, who is said to have been a just and perfect man in his generations (Genesis 6:9), and Lot, whom the Apostle Peter designates by the name of the just (2 Peter 2:7–8), and Joseph of Arimathea (Luke 23:50).
pass_b_english: Scripture often names believers just and holy over against the wicked.
Noah, Lot, Joseph of Arimathea are singled out as just.
